dict.string: Paya connects to your Bluetooth heart rate monitor to track live intensity during training sessions.
Paya reads your calendar events to show them alongside your health data on the Personal Health Management timeline.
Paya uses your camera to scan barcodes and nutrition labels and to photograph meals. If you use AI food recognition, the meal photo is sent to Google Gemini to estimate calories and protein.
Paya accesses your photo library so you can save and review progress photos over time.
Paya uses your location to show local weather conditions on the Personal Health Management timeline — for example, whether you walked during sunny hours.

If you turn on air quality alerts in Settings, Paya checks air quality when you move to a new area, even with the app closed, and notifies you if it is poor. Optional and off by default. Your approximate location is sent to the Open-Meteo air-quality service to look up conditions and is not stored by Paya.

Paya reads your sleep, steps, heart rate, heart rate variability, respiratory rate, blood oxygen, wrist temperature, walking steadiness, weight and workouts from Apple Health to personalize your training, recovery and nutrition targets. This is wellness information, not medical advice.
Paya writes your logged weight and completed workouts to Apple Health so they stay in sync with your other apps.
Paya uses motion data as a fallback to estimate steps and sleep when Apple Health data is unavailable.
Paya uses your microphone only while you dictate a food description, so you can log by voice instead of typing.
Paya uses Apple's speech recognition to turn your spoken food description into text; for AI nutrition estimates that text is sent to Google Gemini.
